t.1.30.1: Then Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the two heroes, having accomplished their purpose, spent that night there, joyful, with their inner selves delighted.
t.1.30.2: When the night had brightened into dawn, the two, having performed their morning rites, went together to Viśvāmitra and the other sages.
t.1.30.3: Having saluted the best of sages, who blazed like fire, the two sweet-spoken ones addressed him with words both sweet and noble.
t.1.30.4: O tiger among sages, here we two stand before you as your servants. Command us as you wish; what order shall we carry out?
t.1.30.5: When this had been said by the two of them, all the great sages, placing Viśvāmitra at their head, then spoke these words to Rāma.
t.1.30.6: O best of men, a supremely righteous sacrifice is to be held by Janaka, the lord of Mithilā; there we shall go.
t.1.30.7: And you too, tiger among men, will go along with us; there you ought to see that wondrous jewel of a bow.
t.1.30.9: Neither the gods nor the gandharvas, neither the asuras nor the rākṣasas are able to string this bow, and in no way can men do so.
t.1.30.8: For that bow, O best of men, was given long ago by the gods in the assembly at a sacrifice; it is of immeasurable strength, terrible, and supremely radiant.
t.1.30.10: Indeed, kings and mighty princes, desiring to test the strength of that bow, were unable to string it.
t.1.30.11: There, O tiger among men, O Kākutstha, you will see that bow of the great-souled Maithila, and also the sacrifice, wondrous to behold.
t.1.30.13: Having spoken thus, the best of sages then set out, together with the host of seers and with the Kākutstha, after bidding farewell to the deities of the forest.
t.1.30.12: For that excellent bow with its beautiful grip, O tiger among men, was the fruit of a sacrifice; it was requested by that lord of Mithilā and granted by all the deities.
t.1.30.14: May it be well with you all. Having achieved my purpose, I shall go from Siddhāśrama to Himavant, the towering mountain, on the northern bank of the Jāhnavī.
t.1.30.15: Then, having circumambulated the incomparable Siddhāśrama, he turned toward the northern direction and began to set out.
t.1.30.16: As that best of sages set out, a train of carts numbering a full hundred, belonging to his followers, the expounders of Brahman, went after him on their journey.
t.1.30.17: And the flocks of beasts and birds dwelling in Siddhāśrama also followed the great-souled Viśvāmitra, the great sage.
t.1.30.18: Having travelled a long way, as the sun was sinking low, those hosts of sages, composed in mind, made their halt on the bank of the Śoṇā.
t.1.30.19: When the sun had set, those men of boundless energy bathed and made offerings into the fire, and then, placing Viśvāmitra before them, they sat down.
t.1.30.20: Rāma too, together with Saumitri, having honoured those sages, then sat down in front of the wise Viśvāmitra.
t.1.30.21: Then Rāma, of great splendour, filled with curiosity, questioned Viśvāmitra, the great sage, the tiger among sages.
t.1.30.22: O blessed one, what is this region, adorned with flourishing forests? I wish to hear it; may good fortune be yours; you should tell me truly.
t.1.30.23: Urged by Rāma's words, the great ascetic, firm in his vows, told in full, in the midst of the sages, all about that region.
